assembly.name: Engine — ancillaries, lubrication & mounts
assembly.description: The dossier §2 items the coverage audit caught, plus the lubrication area built out after the operator's car developed an upper-sump oil leak (2026-08) and then corrected against the R1 research return: the structural aluminium upper sump (which also clamps the main-bearing caps), the RUBBER-gasketed joint to the plastic lower pan, the two-stage oil pump, pickup, bayonet drain plug, G266 sensor and the filter housing/oil cooler above — the leak paths that look identical once oil has run down the block. Also the FEAD belt driving alternator and A/C (the coolant pump is balance-shaft driven), starter, valve cover with the failure-prone PCV diaphragm, coil-on-plug ignition, and the three-point engine mounting.

parts.name: Camshaft bearing bridge / cam carrier
parts.description: R2 CORRECTION: the Gen 3 'valve cover' is really the camshaft bearing bridge/ladder (06K103144D; variants -A/-B, later 06L103144H) sealed to the head with ANAEROBIC SEALANT (VW D174003M2) — there is no conventional cover-plus-gasket. A 'valve cover leak' therefore means removing the bridge, cleaning both faces and re-sealing with new one-time-use bolts, not a gasket swap. The AVS actuators, coils and the bolt-on PCV module mount through/on it.

torqueSpec.note: erWin snippet — renew bolts, diagonal in stages. DISAGREEMENT: Spoolas generic table says M6=10/M7=15/M8=20 Nm; treat 8 Nm + 90° as head-specific pending the manual's full table (R2)

knownIssues: Sealant-surface degradation → oil weep — with the PCV diaphragm, one of the two most likely explanations R2 gives for the operator's oil leak.

parts.name: Ignition coils (coil-on-plug) ×4
parts.description: Pencil coils down the plug wells, one per cylinder, firing order 1-3-4-2. R2: the VW dealer catalogue shows 06H905110P for the Golf R while the GTI/family is frequently 06K905110K — confirm against this car's VIN before ordering. Hold-down ~10 Nm.
knownIssues: Misfires — coils are a common wear item on tuned EA888s (R2).

parts.name: FEAD serpentine belt, pulleys & tensioner
parts.description: Single serpentine belt on the accessory end with automatic tensioner, driving the alternator and A/C compressor only — the EA888 Gen 3's coolant pump is driven off a balance shaft instead (dossier §2, an easy trap when tracing the belt).

parts.name: Alternator
parts.description: Belt-driven alternator with energy-recuperation logic for the start-stop system (dossier §7 battery/charging).

parts.name: A/C compressor
parts.description: Belt-driven A/C compressor low on the accessory end; its refrigerant lines join the HVAC loop in Phase 7 (dossier §8).

parts.name: Starter motor
parts.description: Starter on the block/bellhousing flange, pinion engaging the flywheel ring gear inside the DSG bellhousing (dossier §2).

parts.name: Engine mount, right (hydraulic)
parts.description: Right-side hydraulic (pendulum-type) engine mount on the accessory end, to the body rail. Dossier §2 torques: mount-to-engine-bracket ~60 Nm +90°, mount-to-frame-rail ~40 Nm +90°.

parts.name: Transmission mount, left
parts.description: Left-side mount on top of the DQ250 case to the body rail — the second point of the three-point transverse mounting (dossier §2).

torqueSpec.note: Same MQB mount torque family as the engine side (dossier §2)

parts.name: Dogbone / pendulum support mount
parts.description: The lower torque arm from the gearbox down to the front subframe — third point of the mounting triangle, taking drive-torque rock (dossier §2). The classic first upgrade for sloppy-feeling shifts.

parts.name: Upper sump (die-cast aluminium, structural)
parts.description: The structural upper half of the two-piece sump (R1: 06K103603BL, supersedes 06K103603AN/AP). Far more than an oil pan: it carries the two-stage oil pump, the honeycomb pickup, the windage baffle AND the upper main-bearing supports — bolting up from below it clamps the five main caps, acting as a partial bedplate. Sealed to the block with LIQUID SEALANT and single-use aluminium bolts (torque not captured in R1 — confirm in erWin). THIS is the area the operator's garage identified as leaking (2026-08).
knownIssues: Oil leaks here have three look-alike sources once oil has run down the casting: (a) the sealant joint to the block, (b) the rubber-gasketed joint to the lower pan, (c) oil dripping DOWN from the filter housing / oil cooler above (dossier §2 names those weeps, and rear-main seeps, explicitly). Clean and re-inspect before resealing anything.
Sealant joint weeps with age/heat cycles; aluminium bolts pull threads if over-torqued (R1).

parts.name: Lower sump gasket (rubber, Elring)
parts.description: R1 CORRECTION to our earlier assumption: the joint between the upper and lower sump uses a real RUBBER GASKET (06K103649H, also -J) — not a sealant bead. The liquid-sealant joint is one level up, where the aluminium upper sump meets the block. So a lower-pan reseal is a gasket swap; a block-joint reseal means dropping the upper sump, cleaning both faces and re-applying sealant.
knownIssues: Weep if the gasket is reused (R1) — always fit a new one when the lower pan comes off.

parts.name: Lower sump pan (glass-filled plastic)
parts.description: The plastic lower pan (R1: 06K103600D, also -R/-AE) bolting to the aluminium upper section with the rubber gasket and steel bolts at 8 Nm + 45°. Houses the G266 oil-level/thermal sensor and the quarter-turn bayonet drain plug.
knownIssues: Cracks on impact/curbing — it is plastic and low (R1); a steel-pan upgrade exists aftermarket.
Drain-plug boss strip is a common complaint (R1).

parts.name: Lower sump perimeter bolts (steel)
parts.description: Steel perimeter bolts clamping the plastic lower pan and its rubber gasket to the aluminium upper sump. R1 verified the figure: 8 Nm + 45° (ECS install instructions + VW Vortex DIY + erWin). No numbered sequence is published — work alternately across the joint. NOTE the upper sump's own aluminium bolts to the block are a different, single-use fastener with no captured torque.

torqueSpec.note: Lower pan to upper sump — R1-verified (ECS + VW Vortex + erWin); no numbered sequence published

parts.name: Oil pickup (honeycomb)
parts.description: The honeycomb pickup drawing oil from the pan floor to the two-stage pump — carried by the aluminium upper sump as part of the pump assembly (R1). Its interface seals with the N0282222 O-ring. Inspect the screen for sludge whenever the pan is off: a blocked pickup starves the pump, the jets and the bearings.
knownIssues: Screen sludge blockage (R1) — the quiet killer behind spun bearings and jet blockage.

parts.name: Drain plug (plastic quarter-turn bayonet)
parts.description: R1 CORRECTION: the Gen 3 OEM drain plug is a PLASTIC quarter-turn bayonet in the plastic pan — not a threaded steel plug with a crush washer. No separate part number found (integral to the 06K103600D pan area). OEM plastic-plug torque UNVERIFIED; the common aftermarket steel-pan conversion uses a conventional 30 Nm steel plug.
knownIssues: Cross-thread/strip and leaks are a common complaint with the plastic bayonet design (R1/SSP) — hence the popular steel-pan upgrade.

parts.name: Oil filter housing & oil cooler
parts.description: Filter housing with the oil-to-coolant cooler, and the mount for solenoid N522. OPERATOR-CONFIRMED position (2026-08-15, checked at the car): OFFSIDE (driver's side), the opposite side to the air filter box and the same side as the coolant tank and brake fluid reservoir, high up just inboard of the engine cover edge and directly above the alternator — you reach it from above, and its black hex cap has 25 Nm moulded into it. Because it sits ABOVE the sump, a weep here runs down the block and pools on the sump flange — the single most common reason an upper-sump leak is misdiagnosed (dossier §2 names filter-housing/oil-cooler weeps directly). R9: cooler is integral to the housing, family 06L117021 (VIN-verify).

torqueSpec.note: Filter cap — PHOTO-VERIFIED: 25 Nm is moulded into the cap on the operator's own car (IMG_7691)

knownIssues: Oil-cooler / filter-housing weeps are on the dossier's known-issues list (§2). Because it drips downward onto the sump area, ALWAYS rule this out before resealing a sump.

parts.name: Oil level / thermal sensor G266
parts.description: The G266 oil-level/thermal sensor integrated in the plastic lower pan (R1), feeding level and temperature to the cluster and ECU. Its seal (with the N0282222 O-ring family) is another small leak path.

parts.name: Oil pump, regulated two-stage
parts.description: Chain-driven, electronically regulated two-stage oil pump living in the upper sump (R1). Low stage saves fuel; the N428 valve controls regulation, and a second pressurised gallery feeds the switchable piston-cooling jets. R1 lists 06L115105 / 06K115105-series bins — verify against a live CJXC catalogue before ordering. Pump-to-block bolts 8 Nm + 90°.
knownIssues: Chain wear rare on Gen 3; the real risk is pickup-screen sludge blockage (R1).

parts.name: Oil pressure regulation valve N428
parts.description: The solenoid switching the two-stage pump between low and high pressure, on the oil-pan top section (R1: 06L115243-series — verify exact number).
knownIssues: Sticking valve → oil-pressure faults / warning light (R1).

parts.name: Piston-cooling jet control valve N522
parts.description: Solenoid on the oil-filter/adapter housing gating oil to the piston-jet switching valve (R1; supersedes 06K115243T). Behind its fine screen is where sludge does damage.
knownIssues: Screen clog → 'piston cooling nozzle circuit' high/low DTC and hot pistons (R1).

parts.name: Windage tray / oil baffle
parts.description: The baffle plate calming the oil surface against crank windage and cornering slosh — supplied WITH the upper oil pan, not separately (R1). Baffle bolts 4 Nm + 45° into the aluminium pan top.

torqueSpec.note: Baffle bolt into aluminium pan top (R1)

parts.name: Pickup / level-sensor O-ring
parts.description: The lower oil-pan sealing O-ring at the pickup / level-sensor interface (R1). Small, cheap, and yet another candidate 'sump leak'.
knownIssues: Weep (R1) — renew whenever the pan is off.

parts.name: PCV / oil separator module
parts.description: The crankcase-ventilation/oil-separator module — a SEPARATE bolt-on unit sitting on TOP of the cam cover — PHOTO-VERIFIED on this car: the round black diaphragm dome sits mid-cover, slightly toward the PASSENGER (nearside) half, with the four ignition coils in a row BEHIND it (toward the bulkhead), the HPFP to its right and the oil-filler cap to its left; its breather line runs back toward the turbo (FCP Euro; 7× T30 screws). Lift the plastic engine cover off its ball mounts and it's the first thing you see. Revision chain 06K103495 → AC/AH → AP → BK → BL → BM, each fighting diaphragm rupture and cornering carry-over — owners retrofit the BL/BM or later Gen 4 evo unit. Seal 06E103484-series, renew on R&R. R2's advice for the operator's leak: test/replace this FIRST, then re-seal the cam bridge if the leak persists.
knownIssues: Diaphragm rupture → whistle, rough idle, boost/vacuum faults, oil pushed past seals (rear main especially), smoking under hard cornering — the classic Gen 3 PCV failure (R2, and the dossier's §2 list).

parts.name: Oil filler cap
parts.description: The black screw cap you pour oil into, on top of the cam cover at the OFFSIDE (driver's-side) end — photo-verified on the operator's car, the one with the yellow oil-can symbol and the Castrol recommendation ring. It is also your free diagnostic tool: with the engine idling, lift it. A healthy engine gives light resistance; strong suction that grabs the cap and changes the idle means the PCV diaphragm has torn. Side operator-confirmed 2026-08-15: driver's side (offside) — opposite the air filter box.
knownIssues: A perished cap O-ring weeps oil down the cam cover and gets blamed on the cover seal.
Cross-threading it on a hot engine is easy — it only needs a quarter turn to seat.

parts.name: Brake vacuum pump
parts.description: Camshaft-driven vacuum pump bolted to the end face of the cylinder head — it makes the vacuum your brake servo runs on, which is why a failing one gives a hard brake pedal as well as an oil leak. It shares engine oil, so its gasket (06H103121J) sits between pressurised oil and the outside world, and it appears in every EA888 Gen 3 reseal kit. POSITION IS AN ESTIMATE: placed at the offside (belt) end of the head because the chain and cam drive are at the gearbox end — not yet photo-confirmed on this car, so check yours before ordering (logged in docs/UNVERIFIED.md).
knownIssues: Gasket weep runs down the back of the head and along the block — from below it looks exactly like a rear main seal leak, which is the expensive misdiagnosis.
A worn pump gives a hard/high brake pedal, especially on the first press after start.

parts.name: Oil filter housing / cooler gasket
parts.description: The joint between the filter housing / oil cooler and the block: a perimeter gasket plus the O-rings around the oil feed and return ports. Full oil-pump pressure sits behind this face, so when it goes it does not weep, it runs — straight down the back of the block onto the bellhousing and the sump flange. Modelled as the seal itself rather than the metal so that highlighting it shows the actual leak path.
knownIssues: Runs down onto the bellhousing and gets mistaken for a rear main seal — always clean this joint and re-check before quoting a gearbox-out job.
The cooler side is oil-to-coolant: a failure here can also push oil into the coolant or coolant into the oil (mayonnaise under the filler cap).
